learningObjectives: Choose suitable Java collection types for different data requirements.
Use List, Set, Map, and Queue implementations effectively.
Apply generics to create type-safe collection-based code.

activities.title: Collection Behavior Map
activities.instruction: Explore how the major collection interfaces organize data.

content.concept: The Java Collections Framework provides interfaces and implementations for common data structures. List preserves an ordered sequence, Set represents unique elements, Map associates keys with values, and Queue models elements waiting to be processed.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Collection Matcher
activities.instruction: Choose a suitable collection for each requirement.

content.concept: Collection choice depends on requirements such as duplicates, ordering, key-based lookup, and processing order. ArrayList, HashSet, HashMap, and ArrayDeque are common implementations for different needs.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Generic Type Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore how generic type parameters make collections type-safe.

content.concept: Generics specify the type of elements a generic class or method can work with. For example, List<String> allows the compiler to enforce that the list is intended for String elements.

activities.title: Collection Builder
activities.instruction: Build the collection declaration that fits each scenario.

content.concept: Selecting a collection requires understanding its behavioral requirements. Use a List for ordered duplicates, a Set for uniqueness, a Map for key-value lookup, and a Queue or Deque when processing order matters.
